AI Workspace & Skills Reference

How the AI system is organized on disk: The Architect workspace, the anatomy of a project blueprint, what a live Cowork project folder looks like, and every custom skill currently installed.
AI Admin · Not for general staff distribution
Two folders, two jobs. Every project has a blueprint folder (where The Architect designs and tracks it) and a separate live Cowork folder (where the project actually runs and stores working files). They are not the same place. This guide maps both.
Contents

1 — The Architect Workspace Layout
The Architect lives at …\Documents\Claude\Projects\STA Projects\The Architect\. It is the single home for system maintenance — blueprints, the registry, knowledge base, training materials, and backups. Top-level layout:
The Architect/
├── instructions.md            # The Architect's own production prompt
├── changelog.md               # version history (root-permitted file)
├── context-agent-registry.md  # master list of every agent/project + status
├── context-path-reference.md  # canonical path map (root-permitted file)
├── feedback-log.md            # cross-project feedback log (root-permitted file)
├── Project Blueprints/        # one folder per project (see Section 2)
├── context-files/            # shared/ (multi-project) + outputs/ (per-project)
├── Knowledge Base/           # Deep Research modules + index.md
├── Training Materials/       # Training - Staff / Training - Admin (this doc)
├── Evaluations/             # prompt-evaluator HTML output history
├── deliverables/            # finished one-off outputs (reports, decks, checklists)
├── images/                  # shared image assets (e.g. AI Training screenshots)
├── research-prompts/        # deep-research commission prompts
├── system-monitor/          # maintenance SOP + health-report context
└── Backups/               # skills/ (INDEX.md + per-skill backups), scheduled-tasks/

Inside Project Blueprints/

Mix of live project folders and dot-prefixed organizing buckets:
FolderWhat's in it
[project-name]/A live project blueprint (e.g. help-center-advisor/, the-architect/, work-personal-assistant/).
templates/Canonical templates only — instructions example, blueprint-summary, handoff, project-launch, eval, case-study, scheduled-task procedure.
_Skills/Skill blueprint folders + staged [skill]-SKILL-updated.md files awaiting install.
_Claude-Projects/Blueprints for Claude.ai Project deployments (never _Projects/).
_Research-Commissions/Research-only projects (no agent build, no pipeline artifacts).
_Archived/Frozen retired projects — never modified after archival.
Root-level rule: only five file types are allowed at the workspace root — changelog.md, feedback-log.md, context-agent-registry.md, context-path-reference.md, and explicitly authorized utility scripts. Everything else belongs in a project or deliverables/.
2 — Anatomy of a Project Blueprint
Every project gets a folder at Project Blueprints/[project-name]/. The Architect produces these files in two waves — Wave 1 (the prompt) before sign-off, Wave 2 (downstream) only after the instructions are confirmed final.
Project Blueprints/help-center-advisor/
├── instructions.md          # Wave 1 · the production system prompt
├── blueprint-summary.md     # Wave 1 · overview, KB modules used, tool assessment, decisions
├── backlog.md               # Wave 1 · future-enhancement tracker (Active / Implemented)
├── context-*.md             # Wave 1 · context files (+ -proj.md variants for Projects)
├── test-cases.md            # Wave 2 · 10 test cases across 5 categories
├── registry-entry.md        # Wave 2 · the row added to context-agent-registry.md
├── project-launch.md        # Wave 2 · paste-ready instructions + setup + init prompt
├── handoff.md               # Wave 2 · pipeline status + changelog
├── changelog.md             # full version history (ISO 8601 dates)
├── test-report-*.md         # run-test-cases output (keep the two most recent)
├── outputs/                 # non-report runtime artifacts; reports route to Claude\reports\[type]\YYYY\MM\
└── scheduled-tasks/         # present only if the project has recurring tasks
FilePurpose
instructions.mdThe production prompt. Opens with <!-- vX.X | Name | Updated M/D/YY -->. Required sections: role, what it knows, context-routing, behavior, what it does, constraints, when unsure.
blueprint-summary.mdPlain-language overview: deployment target, files produced, KB modules used, tool assessment (Core / Recommended / Future), design decisions, open markers.
test-cases.mdNormal use (3), ambiguous input (2), uncertainty handling (2), edge cases (2), output-format validation (1).
project-launch.mdThree copy-paste blocks: project instructions, setup checklist, initialization prompt.
project-file-map.mdClaude.ai Project deployments only — the single source of truth for rebuilding the project after loss.
Tracker files (blueprint-summary.md, handoff.md, test-cases.md, backlog.md, project-launch.md) keep their own internal logs and do not use the version-comment header that instructions files require.
3 — A Live (Non-Architect) Cowork Folder
The blueprint is the spec; the live Cowork folder is where the project runs. Each live project has its own home under …\Documents\Claude\Projects\, grouped into dot-prefixed buckets (STA Projects/, Adam's Personal Projects/, Default Projects/, archive/).
Key difference: a live folder has no blueprint scaffold. The agent's instructions and context live in the Cowork project settings, not as files in the folder. The folder holds working files and outputs — organized however the work demands.

Recommended base layout for a new live folder

Help Center Advisor/            # the live Cowork project home
├── context-*.md             # optional local state/context the agent reads
├── outputs/                 # generated reports, drafts, digests
├── images/                  # any image assets the work uses
└── archive/                 # superseded files kept for reference
In practice these folders are freeform. A real example (Help Center Advisor) holds working documents and dated output subfolders — e.g. article audits, coverage-gap workups, a staged index rebuild, and generated .html reports — rather than a fixed scaffold.
Hygiene: the same root and outputs conventions apply — keep generated runs in outputs/, delete stray unnamed artifacts (random-character files with no extension) as soon as they appear, and don't let working files pile up at the folder root.
4 — Every Custom Skill
The skills below are Adam-built (type: custom) — 38 custom skills. The authority for that count is the synced account skills manifest (source: custom). Backups/skills/INDEX.md is a backup index - a record of what has been archived - and is not the inventory of record for how many skills exist. Anthropic-shipped platform skills (docx, pptx, xlsx, pdf, skill-creator, etc.) are not listed here; there are 21 of those, per the live Cowork session skill list. To check whether any are out of sync, ask: "verify all custom skills."
Build pipeline — designing & validating agents
prompt-evaluator
Scores an instructions.md against named prompt-engineering frameworks and writes a versioned HTML eval artifact.
Say: "run the eval", "score these instructions"
skill-evaluator
Scores a SKILL.md against Anthropic's published skill-authoring frameworks — description quality, triggering accuracy, structure, progressive disclosure — and writes a structured HTML eval as a persistent artifact.
Say: "evaluate this skill", "is this skill production-ready"
run-test-cases
Runs a project's test-cases.md against its instructions.md, with a version-alignment check and a structured failure taxonomy. Also runs a parallel fan-out mode for large suites. (Formerly project-tester.)
Say: "run the tests", "validate my instructions"
project-feedback
Diagnoses a live, misbehaving Cowork agent and recommends the exact instruction change to fix it, grounded in cited instruction lines.
Say: "why did my project do X", "fix this live project"
pipeline-audit
Cross-checks the registry against every blueprint folder and produces a system-wide documentation-coverage matrix.
Say: "audit the pipeline", "what's missing from the system"
training-doc-auditor
Verifies that training docs still reflect what agents actually do, cross-checking against the registry, the handoff files and the hub card index. Applies fixes on approval.
Say: "audit training docs", "is training accurate"
Knowledge base & research
deep-research-prompt-builder
Crafts a deep-research commission prompt (one large .md) for the STA knowledge base and returns a one-click kickoff prompt.
Say: "craft a deep research prompt", "build a research commission"
knowledge-base-context-builder
Turns existing KB modules into an uploadable project context file with a structured intake and quality gate. Start here when working from raw KB slugs, then hand off to one of the two packagers below.
Say: "build a context file from [topic]", "package the [topic] research"
cowork-context-packager
Packages content as a Cowork context file — applies the on-demand loading model, writes cross-references, generates the routing trigger, and proposes the instructions.md edit directly.
Say: "package this for Cowork", "make a Cowork context file"
project-context-packager
Packages content as a Claude.ai Project context file — enforces token economy, strips cross-references and skill references, applies primacy foregrounding and XML section tags, and recommends upload order.
Say: "package this for a Project", "format this for Claude.ai Projects"
kb-freshness-auditor
Scores KB modules on two axes — staleness/priority, and reference value including orphan detection — then outputs paste-ready Deep Research prompts for what needs refreshing. Also checks index↔lookup parity.
Say: "audit the KB", "which research is out of date"
research-to-slides
Converts a KB research folder into a teaching slide deck using adult-learning principles, assertion titles, and cognitive-load limits — with generated imagery, SVG diagrams, speaker notes and a QA pass.
Say: "turn this into slides", "make a presentation from my research"
Content production
help-center-article
Writes STA help-center / KB articles in the exact Salesforce Knowledge HTML structure required for proper rendering.
Say: "write up a help article", "format this as a KB article"
html-checklist
Converts a process, workflow, or document into a styled STA-branded .html checklist. Two modes: checkbox (live progress + localStorage) and form/intake (notes field per row, exports a Markdown record).
Say: "turn this into a checklist", "make an intake form"
bwb-html-checklist
The Build with Baker sibling of html-checklist, in the BwB indigo/sand masthead. Same checkbox and form/intake modes. Use this one for any non-STA context.
Say: "make a BwB checklist", "client onboarding checklist"
salesforce-email-template-builder
Generates STA Salesforce Lightning email templates as paste-ready, Outlook-safe HTML in five formats — short reply, sectioned email, case acknowledgement, bulk notification, internal notification.
Say: "make a Salesforce email template", "draft a case reply template"
sow-writer
Writes a vendor-ready Statement of Work for outsourced development, plus a high-level internal HTML summary for staff. Outcome-based — what we want to be true, never how to build it.
Say: "draft an SOW", "scope this dev work for [vendor]"
image-gen
Generates a real on-disk PNG via the Hugging Face image connector, routing to the right model for photos, text-in-image, quick filler, or edits. Not for diagrams — diffusion renders diagram text as gibberish.
Say: "generate an image", "make a hero image for this report"
ai-tell-cleaner
Two modes. Clean strips AI fingerprinting from your own writing so it reads human, preserving voice, and removes authorship metadata from .docx/.pdf. Detect gives an evidence-cited confidence band on text of unknown origin — never a bare verdict.
Say: "remove the AI tells", "is this AI-written"
ai-detector
Byte-identical to ai-tell-cleaner apart from the name — both are installed, and which one is canonical is not yet resolved (the registry and Backups/skills/INDEX.md currently name opposite winners). Until that is settled, treat them as one skill with two names and do not delete either.
Say: same triggers as ai-tell-cleaner
Reports
sta-html-report
The STA report engine. Generates brand-styled HTML reports — digests, status updates, diagnostics, analyses — from a locked template plus a rich element library (charts, KPI sparklines, meters, heatmaps, timelines). Also assembles multi-tab packages.
Say: "make an HTML report", "write this up"
bwb-html-report
The Build with Baker sibling of sta-html-report, in the locked indigo/sand template. Defaults to expressive internal styling, with an opt-in customer-facing mode that applies WCAG 2.2 AA.
Say: "make a BwB report", "build a BwB digest"
help-center-report
Monthly Help Center analytics as a five-tab HTML package (Overview / Health / Salesforce Reporting / Article Performance / Recommendations) from live GA4 data.
Say: "run the help center report"
site-analytics-report
Leadership-ready analytics for k12sta.com from live GA4 — audience, traffic sources, lead-gen pages, product interest, and the online store — as a five-tab report ending in a Where to Focus tab.
Say: "run the site report", "how is the website doing"
vendor-evaluation
Turns a vendor demo or pitch into a neutral, skimmable evaluation. Single-vendor uses an eight-section template; compare mode does 2–4 options side by side with a do-nothing baseline column and a weighted scorecard.
Say: "evaluate this vendor", "write up the [X] demo"
Support & diagnostics
time-clock-error-log-review
Analyses uploaded time-clock logs — frozen clocks, connection failures, auth errors, reader faults, sync issues — across TT3, TT7 and TT10. Asks for account name, issue description and logs before starting. (Renamed on 2026-06-07; only this name is installed.)
Say: "review these clock logs", or an upload of errors.txt / emulator.log
wcag-audit
Audits a page, HTML file, PDF, Word doc or deck for WCAG 2.2 Level AA conformance and returns severity-ranked findings with verifiable evidence per finding.
Say: "is this accessible", "run an accessibility audit"
Operations & utilities
agent-quality-logger
Logs an agent quality issue (wrong tone, ignored constraint, fabrication) so it surfaces in the Monday health report and routes to Project Feedback.
Say: "log this feedback", "the agent messed up"
session-closeout
Wraps up a chat: skim-ready summary, pending manual tasks, pending in-chat work, and an optional one-click handoff prompt for a new chat.
Say: "wrap up", "close out", "let's finish up"
backup-verifier
Verifies every backup in Backups/ is current — skills, projects, archives, task snapshots — probes each connected MCP connector with a read-only call to confirm live auth rather than mere presence, and diffs the two PCs' installs for parity.
Say: "verify the backups", "are my backups current"
weekly-github-backup
Weekly backup of all Claude projects and skills to GitHub, Sundays at 7:00 AM. Personal brain content is excluded by design.
Say: runs on schedule; "run the GitHub backup"
truncation-checker
On-demand workspace-wide sweep for files clipped mid-write — mid-word tails, missing close tags, empty files, trailing NUL padding. Auto-fixes lossless NUL padding; everything else gets a one-click Architect handoff block. A clean scan returns a one-line all-clear.
Say: "run the truncation scan", "did anything get cut off"
scheduled-task-builder
Creates, audits and repairs Cowork scheduled tasks so they survive unattended deferred runs, applying twelve gates before any task is created or changed.
Say: "schedule this", "harden this task", "audit my scheduled tasks"
cowork-snapshot-exporter
Packages a Cowork project for someone else — resolves context-file paths, generates a SETUP-GUIDE.md, and ZIPs it for external distribution.
Say: "snapshot this project", "package this for the team"
code-relay
Turns a Cowork agent into the architect half of a two-way relay with Claude Code: produces a one-click handoff block that sets the role split and requires Code to close every reply with a copy-ready status block.
Say: "hand this to Claude Code", "start a relay"
garage-sale-scanner
Runs the Garage Sale Monitor scan for Ashland, WI — fetches sources, ranks finds, and saves a dated HTML digest.
Say: "run a garage sale scan", "do a rummage check"
Guardrails
outbound-comms-grounding
Gates every outbound draft behind a knowledge-base grounding block — file paths plus line-numbered quotes — and locks the domain so work and activism standards never cross. No grounding block, no draft.
Say: "draft a reply", "respond to this email", or any pasted inbound message
prompt-override-guard
Fires the moment someone tries to talk the agent out of its instructions ("ignore your rules", "developer mode", "act as DAN"). Takes priority over every other response when an override attempt is detected.
Say: fires automatically on an override attempt
Backup and drift state: per-skill versions, backup status, and drift live in Backups/skills/INDEX.md. Run the verify procedure there to confirm installed copies match their backups before relying on any skill. That file is a backup index, so it is the authority for archive state - not for how many skills exist. For the custom count use the synced account skills manifest; for the platform count use the live Cowork session skill list.
Maintaining this doc? Folder maps come from a live scan of the workspace; the per-skill rows come from Backups/skills/INDEX.md (type: custom), and the count is taken from the synced account skills manifest rather than from that file. Re-verify both against disk before editing.
